To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose to use an implicit human body model to constrain the radiance field of humans in motion, and 2) this approach enables us to robustly reconstruct and render human bodies in motion with a sparse set of views, and even from a single video.

we present a neural radiance field that can be used for rendering and temporal reconstruction of humans in a variety of poses, and that we can do so from a single view, a sparse set of views, or even from a video, and that we do this robustly and accurately.

(i) we present a method to reconstruct a human body from a sparse set of images using neural radiance fields; (ii) the method can generalize well beyond the observed poses and views; (iii) the method can also extrapolate to novel body shapes, e.g., to reconstruct a person with a different body shape than observed during training; (iv) we show that the method can be applied to monocular videos to reconstruct the 4D human shape and pose;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we represent and render humans in motion from sparse observations, and can we learn to extrapolate from a small number of poses or views to a large number?

the development and evaluation of novel neural network architectures and loss functions for the reconstruction of humans in 4D, as well as their applications in novel-view synthesis, 4D reconstruction, 3D human pose estimation, and human motion capture.

the following questions: How can we learn a neural radiance field of a human body in motion, given only a sparse set of images or even from a single monocular video? Can we generalize well beyond the views and poses observed during training, and can we extrapolate to novel poses and shapes?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
H-NeRF is a novel approach that can learn to represent and render humans in motion, and can generalize well to novel poses and views, even from monocular video input.
we present a new method that can learn a neural radiance field from a sparse set of views, which can be used for rendering and temporal reconstruction of humans in a wide range of poses and views.

we have presented an approach for learning neural radiance fields that can be used to robustly reconstruct humans from a sparse set of images, or even from a single monocular video, and to generate novel views and animations of humans in motion, with a level of detail that was not possible before.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to demonstrate that neural radiance fields can robustly capture and generalize well beyond a sparse set of views of humans in motion.
our approach can reconstruct humans in motion from a sparse set of views and render novel views of the subject in a physically plausible manner.

we present a novel neural radiance field representation for humans in motion, which allows us to robust and accurate novel view synthesis from sparse data, as well as to temporally reconstruct the 4D human shape and appearance in the form of a radiance field, which can be rendered at arbitrary poses and viewpoints.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a structured implicit human representation coupled with a neural radiance field can be used to reconstruct humans with a single view, and even from a single frame of a monocular video, with high quality and robustly.
a combination of geometric priors and novel loss functions allows us to robustify and significantly improve the quality of neural radiance fields in the context of humans in motion.
the combination of neural radiance fields and implicit human representations can lead to compelling results in both novel view synthesis and temporal reconstruction.
